newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich says odds of Democratic Congress win slim.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich says odds of Democratic Congress win slim.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Saturday that Democrats have only a one-in-10 chance of recapturing Congress in the November election.

Speaking to reporters during a campaign news conference, the Georgia Republican predicted his party would increase its hold on the House by between six and 30 seats through victories in more than half a dozen states from New Jersey to Texas.
"There's a 10 percent chance we could lose the Congress, just because in the end elections are up to God and the American people, and anything can happen in the age of television," he said.

Gingrich stunned sceptical political pundits two years ago by predicting correctly that Republicans would take over Congress with a campaign based on the party's Contract With America. Weeks later, the Republicans captured both the House and Senate for the first time in 40 years.
Recent polls have indicated that Democrats, buttressed by President Clinton's commanding lead over Republican challenger Bob Dole, could be in position to regain control of Capitol Hill.
The Democratic Party needs to pick up 20 House seats in November to shift the balance of power in the House, where Republicans hold a 235-198 advantage.
